title: US and China explore AI ‘hot line’ amid safety concerns
key_facts: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the US proposed a 'notification mechanism' on AI between the two countries after talks with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng, ahead of a Trump-Xi summit.
He said the goal was 'a shared vision of common goals and common threats', without more detail.

Jean-Marc Rickli of the Geneva Centre for Security compared the idea to the Cold War hot line created after the 1962 Cuban missile crisis, and cited a CNN report that the US military almost boarded a Chinese ship on an incorrect AI-drawn report.
Consultancy Teneo said neither government is yet willing to commit to binding constraints on AI development.

French researcher Mathilde Viellet of IFRI said the two sides differ on safety: China stresses deepfakes and information security, the US worries about loss of control and misalignment; the US prefers proprietary models, China open source.
Rickli said a hot line makes sense in the military sphere but asked whether that is realistic when operational speed is a key advantage.
Matt Sheehan of the Carnegie Endowment said the most important AI governance actions will be domestic, not bilateral agreements.
quote_evidence: The US has proposed that we have a notification mechanism between the two countries
neither government is yet willing to commit to binding constraints on AI development
why_it_matters_hint: A US-China AI hot line would be a first crisis tool for AI, but it is a proposal and experts doubt its reach.
event_date: Talks and Bessent's statement on or before 3 Oct 2026 (article dated 3 Oct 2026).
